**Important legal note – Switzerland (Winterthur)** Under the Swiss Youth Employment Protection Act (Jugendarbeitsschutzgesetz, JArbSchG) a 14‑year‑old may only perform *light* work and is subject to the following limits: | Age | Daily max. | Weekly max. | Allowed working hours | Night‑work ban | |-----|------------|-------------|-----------------------|----------------| | 14‑15 | 8 h | 40 h | Outside school hours (usually after school) | **No work between 20:00 (8 pm) and 06:00 (6 am)** | | 16‑17 | 9 h | 45 h | Same as above | Night work allowed only with special permission (e.g., hospitality) | Because the cafe’s “night” shift would run past 20:00, a 14‑year‑old **cannot legally work until 23:00** on Fridays or Saturdays. Employing him beyond 20:00 would violate youth‑protection rules and could result in fines for the business. --- ### What you can do instead 1. **Shift the evening work earlier** – finish no later than 20:00. 2. **Keep the total hours light** (e.g., 2–4 h per shift) to stay well within the daily/weekly limits. 3. **Obtain written parental consent** (the parents already said they’re fine, but a signed note is advisable). 4. **Register the minor** with the local *Arbeitsamt* (or the cantonal office for youth employment) if required – many cantons need a simple notification for minors working in hospitality. 5. **Provide a break** of at least 30 min if the shift exceeds 4.5 h, and ensure a minimum of 12 h rest between shifts. --- ### Sample compliant schedule (Friday & Saturday) | Day | Start | End | Total hours | Tasks (examples) | |-----|-------|-----|-------------|------------------| | Friday | 16:00 | 20:00 | 4 h | • Setting tables & preparing the dining area
• Light food‑prep (e.g., slicing bread, washing vegetables)
• Taking simple orders at the counter
• Clearing and cleaning tables after guests leave | | Saturday | 16:00 | 20:00 | 4 h | Same as Friday (or rotate tasks to keep it varied) | **Total weekly hours:** 8 h – well under the 40 h weekly ceiling and far below the daily 8 h limit. If you would like a slightly shorter shift (e.g., 2 h) to test how it works, you could schedule: | Day | Start | End | Hours | |-----|-------|-----|-------| | Friday | 17:00 | 19:00 | 2 h | | Saturday | 17:00 | 19:00 | 2 h | Feel free to adjust the start/end times as long as the shift ends **no later than 20:00** and the total daily hours stay ≤ 8 h. --- ### Quick checklist before the first shift - [ ] Written parental consent (signed and dated). - [ ] Notification to the cantonal youth‑employment office (if required). - [ ] Brief workplace‑safety orientation (e.g., hot‑equipment handling, hygiene). - [ ] Clear list of permitted tasks (no heavy lifting, no operation of dangerous machinery, no serving alcohol). - [ ] Break schedule posted (if shift > 4.5 h). - [ ] End‑of‑shift check‑out time recorded to monitor compliance. By keeping the work within the legal window (ending at 20:00) you’ll give the teenager a safe, lawful earning opportunity while protecting your café from regulatory issues. If you later decide to employ him once he turns 16, you could then consider extending the shift into the evening (subject to the specific permissions for 16‑17‑year‑olds in hospitality). Let me know if you’d like a template for the parental‑consent form or any other paperwork!
